 Judgment

This is petition filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, seeking compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- from the respondents, on account of grievous injuries sustained by the petitioner in road traffic accident.

2. The brief facts of the case are as follows:
On 06-07-2022 at about 12.15 p.m., the petitioner was proceeding on motorcycle bearing No.KA-41-W-5640 as a pillion rider, along with one Kumar as rider, near Srinivasa Nursery, Ketohalli, Tavarekere Hobli, Bengaluru City.

At that time, an auto-rickshaw bearing No.KA-03-AC-9762, being driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner, without observing traffic rules and regulations, came from opposite direction and dashed to the motorcycle of the petitioner.
Due to the said impact, the petitioner and rider fell down on the road and sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately after the accident, the petitioner was shifted to Shreya Hospital,
Bengaluru, wherein he was treated as an in-patient.
Earlier to the accident, he was working as painter and earning Rs.15,000/- per month.
But, due to the accidental injuries, he became permanently disabled and thereby lost his earning capacity.
The Tavarekere Police have registered the case against the driver of the said auto for the offences punishable under Section 279 and 337 of I.P.C.
The respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
Hence, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Therefore, it is prayed to allow the petition and award compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- with interest.
3. On service of notice to the respondents, the respondent No.2 appeared through its counsel and filed the written statement.
Whereas, the respondent No.1 did not choose to appear and remained absent.
Hence, the respondent No.1 is placed as ex-parte.
4. The respondent No.2 in its written statement has denied all the allegations made in the petition.

It has admitted the issuance of "Digit commercial vehicle package policy - passenger carrying vehicle" policy in respect of auto bearing No. KA-03-AC-9762 in favour of respondent No.1 and its validity as on the date of accident.
It seeks protection under Section 147 and 150(2) of Motor Vehicles Act.

It has contended that, the petition is bad for non compliance of provision under Raghu R.L vs Nayazkhan on 8 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/152818485/
2 Sections 134(C) and 158(6) of Motor Vehicles Act.
It has further contended that, the alleged accident has caused due to negligence on the part of rider of motorcycle.
There is delay in lodging the complaint with respect of alleged accident.
No valid reasons are assigned for the delay in lodging the complaint.
The petitioner in order to claim compensation has falsely implicated the auto-rickshaw bearing No.KA-03-AC-9762, in collusion with the insured and the police.
The driver of the offending auto-rickshaw was not holding valid and effective driving licence as on the date of accident.

As such the jurisdictional police have filed charge- sheet under Section 181 of Motor Vehicles Act stating that, the driver of the auto-rickshaw was not holding driving licence to drive the vehicle as on the date of accident.
It has further contended that, the auto-rickshaw was not having valid permit to ply in the place of accident and it is violation of the policy conditions.
It has denied the age, income and avocation of the petitioner, injuries, medical expenses and treatment taken by him.
It has denied the occurrence and mode of accident and also involvement of the auto-rickshaw.
Further, it has sought for permission to contest even on behalf of respondent No.1 as per Section 170 of the Motor Vehicles Act.
Further it is contended that, the compensation claimed is highly excessive and exorbitant.
For the above denials and contentions, it is prayed for dismissal of the petition.

5. On the basis of rival pleadings of both the sides, the following issues are framed:
ISSUES 1.

Whether the petitioner proves that, he has sustained grievous injuries in the Road Traffic Accident, alleged to have occurred on 06-07-2022 at about 12.15 p.m., due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Auto Rickshaw bearing registration No. KA-03-AC-9762 ?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?

If so, what is the quantum and from whom ?
3. What order or Award ?
6.
In order to prove his case, the petitioner has got examined himself as P.W.1 and got marked 8 documents as Ex.P.1 to 8 and closed his side.
On the other hand, the respondents No.2 has examined its official as R.W.1 and got marked one document as Ex.R.1 and closed its side.
7. I have heard the arguments of both the sides and perused the entire material placed on record.

8. My findings on the above issues are as under:
Issue No.1: Partly Affirmative Issue No.2: Partly Affirmative Issue No.3: As per the final order, for the following:
REASONS Raghu R.L vs Nayazkhan on 8 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/152818485/
3 9.

Issue No.1: It is specific case of the petitioner that, on 06-07-2022 at about 12.15 p.m., when he was proceeding on motorcycle bearing No.KA-41-W-5640 as a pillion rider, along with one Kumar as rider, near Srinivasa Nursery, Ketohalli, Tavarekere Hobli, Bengaluru City,

the offending auto-rickshaw bearing No.KA-03-AC-9762, being driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner, without observing traffic rules and regulations, came from opposite direction and dashed to the motorcycle of the petitioner.
Due to the said impact, the petitioner and rider fell down on the road and sustained grievous injuries.
Immediately after the accident, the petitioner was shifted to Shreya Hospital, Bengaluru, wherein he was treated as an in-patient.
Earlier to the accident, he was working as painter and earning Rs.15,000/- per month.
But, due to the accidental injuries, he became permanently disabled and thereby lost his earning capacity.

Further it is contended that,
earlier to the accident, he was working as painter and earning Rs.15,000/- per month.
But, due to the accidental injuries, he became permanently disabled and thereby lost his earning capacity.

10. In order to prove his case, the petitioner has examined himself as P.W.1 by filing examination-in-chief affidavit, wherein he has reiterated entire averments made in the petition and got marked total 8 documents as Ex.P.1 to 8.

Out of the said documents, Ex.P.1 is true copy of F.I.R.,
Ex.P.2 is true copy of first information statement, Ex.P.3 is true copy of charge-sheet, Ex.P.4 is true copy of spot mahazar, Ex.P.5 is true copy of Motor Vehicle Accident report, Ex.P.6 is true copy of wound certificate, Ex.P.7 is OPD record and Ex.P.8 is notarised copy of Aadhar card.

11. On meticulously going through the police documents marked as Ex.P.1 to 6, prima-facia it reveals that, on 06-07- 2022 at about 12.15 p.m., when he was proceeding on motorcycle bearing No.KA-41-W-5640 as a pillion rider, along with one Kumar as rider, near Srinivasa Nursery,
Ketohalli, Tavarekere Hobli, Bengaluru City, the offending auto-rickshaw bearing No.KA-03-AC-9762, being driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner, came from opposite direction and dashed to the motorcycle of the petitioner.

The investigation officer in his final report,
which is marked as Ex.P.3, has clearly stated that, the alleged accident has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of auto-rickshaw bearing Reg. No.KA-03-AC- 9762.
12.

At the outset, it is pertinent to note that, the date, time and place of accident, issuance of insurance policy by the respondent No.2 with respect to auto-rickshaw bearing No.KA-03-AC-9762 and its validity as on the date of accident are not in dispute.

Further, the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner has remained undisputed by the owner of offending vehicle/Respondent No.1, as he did not choose to appear and contest the case of the petitioner.

Whereas, the respondent No.2 insurance company, though has specifically denied the above stated facts in its written statement and taken specific defence that, the said accident is caused due to self negligence on the part of rider of motorcycle and the auto-rickshaw bearing No.KA-03-AC-9762 has been falsely implicated in the case by the petitioner, has not produced any evidence to establish the said contentions.

Except the self serving statements of R.W.1, who is the representative of respondent No.2 insurance company, there is no other rebuttal oral or documentary evidence produced by the respondent No.1 to disprove the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner.

Further, the petitioner/P.W.1, has unequivocally denied the suggestion made by the learned counsel for respondent No.2 that, the alleged accident has caused due to their self negligence and they have lodged false complaint against the driver of auto-rickshaw bearing Raghu R.L vs Nayazkhan on 8 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/152818485/
4 No.KA-03-AC-9762.
Though, the learned counsel for respondent No.2 has cross-examined P.W.1 in length, nothing worth has been elicited from his mouth which creates doubt on the veracity of his evidence.

There is absolutely no evidence on record to show that, the said accident has caused due to negligent riding on the part of the rider of motorcycle bearing No.KA-41-W-5640 and there is no negligence driving on the part of the driver of offending auto-rickshaw bearing No.KA-03-AC-9762.
13.

The Ex.P.4 spot mahazer clearly speaks that, the said accident has taken place on 22 feet wide Ramohalli- Doddaladamara road, near Srinivasa Nursery, Ketohalli, Tavarekere Hobli, Bengaluru City, in between motorcycle bearing No.KA-41-W-5640 and car bearing No.KA-03-AC- 9762.

Further, the damage caused to both the vehicles on the front portion, as noted in the Ex.P.5 Motor Vehicle Accident report, clearly goes to show that, the said accident is caused due to head collusion of both the vehicles.

The investigation officer in his Ex.P.3 final report has clearly stated that, the alleged accident has caused due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of autorickshaw bearing Reg. No. KA-03-AC-9762.
14.
Further, as per the Ex.P.5 Motor Vehicle Accident Report, the accident was not caused due to any mechanical defects in the offending vehicle bearing Reg. No. KA-03-AC- 9762.

When the accident was not due to the any mechanical defects in the offending vehicle and there was no negligence on the part of the rider of motorcycle bearing No.KA-41-W-5640, then in the present facts and circumstances, it can be presumed that, the said accident is caused due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending auto-rickshaw bearing No. KA-03-AC-9762.
Further, admittedly the final report/charge-sheet filed by the investigation officer has not been challenged by the driver or by the owner of offending auto-rickshaw bearing No. KA-03-AC-9762.

In such circumstances, there is no impediment to believe the final report filed by the investigation officer and other police records,
regarding the date, time and place of accident, involvement of offending vehicle in the accident, rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending vehicle and injuries caused to the petitioner in the said accident.

15. Further, the Ex.P.6 wound certificate and Ex.P.7 OPD record clearly speaks that, the petitioner has suffered simple injuries i.e. lacerated wound over right frontal region, pain and swelling over left knee and tenderness left side of chest, in a road traffic accident.
On the other hand, there is no rebuttal evidence produced by the respondents to show that, the above medical records are false created documents.

Therefore, in such circumstances and in the light of above observations, it can safely be held that, the respondent No.2 insurance company has failed to rebut the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner regarding the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the auto-rickshaw bearing Reg. No. KA-03-AC-9762 and injuries caused to the petitioner in the said accident.
There is nothing on record to disbelieve the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner.

16. Further, it is well settled principle of law that, in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims,
the claimants are not required to prove the case as required to be done in a criminal trial.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Parameshwari V/s Amir Chand and others, reported in (2011)
SCC 635, has clearly held that, "in a road accident claim cases the strict principle of proof in a criminal case are not required."

The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of Bimla Devi and others V/s Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others, reported in (2009) 13 SCC 513, has clearly held that, " in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims, the claimants are merely required to establish their case on touch stone of preponderance of probability and the standard of proof on beyond reasonable doubt could not be applied."

sentences.text: 18. Therefore, for the above stated reasons and in the light of observations made in the above cited decisions, this Court is of the considered opinion that, the petitioner has successfully proved that, he has sustained injuries in a motor vehicle accident, occurred on 06-07-2022 at about 12.15 p.m., near Srinivasa Nursery, Ketohalli, Tavarekere Hobli, Bengaluru City, due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of auto-rickshaw bearing Reg. No.KA-03-AC-9762.
But, he has failed to prove that, he has sustained grievous injuries in the said accident.
Hence, I answer Issue No.1 in Partly Affirmative.
19. Issue No.2:

While answering above issue this Court has come to conclusion that, the petitioner has successfully proved that, the accident has caused due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of auto-rickshaw bearing Reg. No.KA-03-AC-9762 and he has sustained simple injuries in the said accident.
The petitioner has sustained lacerated wound over right frontal region, pain and swelling over left knee and tenderness left side of chest.

Therefore, this Court is of the further opinion that,
the petitioner is entitled for compensation under various heads.

The damages are to be assessed under two heads i.e. pecuniary damages, such as medical treatment, attendants, transport, actual loss of earning, future loss of earning etc., and non pecuniary damages, such as mental and physical shock, loss of amenities, loss of expectation of life, loss of prospects of marriage etc.
But, there is no evidence placed on record by the petitioner for the purpose of assessing the above pecuniary and non-pecuniary damages.
In such circumstances, there is no other option before this Court, except to consider global compensation in general.
20. As per Ex.P.6 wound certificate, the petitioner has sustained lacerated wound over right frontal region, pain and swelling over left knee and tenderness left side of chest.
The above said injuries are simple in nature.

The petitioner has deposed that, immediately after the accident, he was shifted to Shreya Hospital, Bengaluru, wherein he took treatment as an inpatient and thereafter he has taken follow up treatment at Jayadevi Memorial Hospital and he has spent Rs.2,00,000/- towards medical expenses.
In order to prove the same, he has not produced any medical bills.
Therefore, the petitioner is not entitled for any compensation under the head of medical expenses.
21. Further, the petitioner has deposed in his evidence that, earlier to the accident he was working as painter and was earning Rs.20,000/- per month.
Due to the accidental injuries, he has become permanently disabled and thereby lost his earning capacity.

But, it is pertinent to note that, the petitioner has neither examined the doctor, nor he has produced any document to show that, he has suffered any permanent physical disability or deformity due to injuries sustained in the accident.
Even he has not produced the discharge summary from the above said hospitals.
Such being the case, it is difficult to ascertain pain and sufferings, laid up period, conveyance charges, loss of amenities etc.

No doubt, due to above injuries the petitioner would have suffered some pain and sufferings and the same would have been nourished with nutritious food, he might have attended with the attendants and he might have spent for conveyance.

In such circumstances, taking into Raghu R.L vs Nayazkhan on 8 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/152818485/
6 consideration the facts and circumstances of the case, even though there is no documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner, taking into consideration the injuries and pains suffered by the petitioner, on humanitarian ground and in general-globally, this Court is of the opinion that,
some suitable compensation is required to be awarded to as he knocked the door of the Court for compensation.

sentences.text: Accordingly, awarding total compensation of Rs.50,000/- to the petitioner, would meet the ends of justice.
22. Liability:
Now the question before this Court is, who is liable to pay the above compensation amount to the petitioner.
Admittedly, as on the date of accident, the respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle.

Further, the evidence placed on record by the petitioner clearly establishes that, due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending auto-rickshaw bearing Reg. No. KA-03-AC-9762 the accident has occurred.

In such circumstances,
the respondent No.1 being the owner of said vehicle is vicariously liable to compensate for the damage caused by the said vehicle.

The respondent No.2 being the insurer of the offending vehicle has to indemnify the respondent No.1.
23.

The learned counsel for respondent No.2 vehemently argued that, the Ex.R.1 Insurance Policy clearly speaks that, the policy covers the risk provided the driver of offending vehicle holds an effective driving licence at the time of accident and is not disqualified from holding or obtaining such a licence.

The Ex.P.3 charge-sheet clearly speaks that, as on the date of accident the accused/driver of the offending auto-rickshaw bearing Reg. No. KA-03-AC-9762 was not holding valid and effective driving licence to drive the said vehicle and hence in addition to the offence punishable under Sec.279, 337 and 338 of I.P.C., he has been charge-sheeted for offence punishable U/Sec.181 of Motor Vehicles Act.
Admittedly, the final report filed by the investigation officer has not been challenged either by the driver of by the owner offending auto-rickshaw.
Even, the petitioner has not produced any document to show that, as on the date of accident the driver of offending auto- rickshaw was holding valid driving licence to drive the said vehicle.

In such circumstances, the respondent No.1/owner of offending vehicle, who has consciously handed over his vehicle to a person who did not possess driving licence to drive the said vehicle, cannot be permitted to take the benefit of his wrong and the respondent No.2/Insurance Company is entitled to raise a defence under Sec.149(2) of Motor Vehicles Act.

In support of his arguments, he has relied on the following decisions:
i) Beli Ram V/s Rajinder Kumar and another, reported in AIR 2020 SC 4453.
ii) Hemalatha @ Hema @ Hemavathi W/o Renukappa and others V/s Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Company and another, in MFA No.6154/2019 (MV-D), judgment dated 14-12-2023.
iii) Smt. Adilakshmammama W/o Late Venkateshappa and others V/s Sri Raju B. S/o Balaraju and another, in MFA No.3297/2019 (MV-D), judgment dated 13-04-2023.
24.

On the other hand, the learned counsel for petitioner vehemently argued that, it is settled principle of law that, the insurance company is liable to pay the third party and recover from the insured even if there is breach of any condition recognised under Sec.149(2) of Motor Vehicles Act,
Raghu R.L vs Nayazkhan on 8 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/152818485/
7 even if it is fundamental breach.

In support of his arguments, he has relied on the following decisions:
 i) The Legal Manager, Sriram General  Insurance Company Ltd. V/s Smt.
 Nagamma, in MFA No.7089/2016 (MV-  D) C/w MFA No. 6824/2016, judgment  dated 19-09-2024.
ii) New India Assurance Co. Ltd., Bijapur by its Divisional Manager V/s Yallavva and another,
reported in ILR 2020 Kar 2239.
25.

sentences.text: Admittedly, in the instant case, as on the date of alleged accident the driver of the offending auto-rickshaw bearing Reg. No. KA-03-AC-9762 was not holding valid and effective driving licence to drive the said vehicle.

Further, there is no evidence on record to show that, before handing over the offending vehicle to his driver/accused, the respondent No.1 was not aware or he was not conscious that his driver was not holding valid driving licence to drive the said vehicle.
Even, there is no document produced to show that, the offending vehicle was having valid permit as on the date of accident, to ply the said vehicle in the place of accident.

In such circumstances and for the above stated reasons, this Court is of the opinion that, the arguments advanced by the learned counsel for petitioner does not hold good and the ratio laid down in the above cited decisions, relied by him, is not applicable to the case in hand.

On the other hand, the arguments advanced by the learned counsel for respondent No.2 hold good and the ratio laid down in the above cited decisions, relied by him, is aptly applicable to the case in hand.

Therefore, for the above stated reasons and in the light of ratio laid down in the above cited decision, this Court comes to conclusion that, the respondent No.1 being the owner of offending vehicle is liable to pay the above compensation amount to the petitioner.

As there is fundamental breach of insurance policy conditions by the respondent No.1,
the respondent No.2 insurance company is not liable to indemnify the respondent No.1.

Further, as the cause of action for filing the present claim petition has arose after coming into force of Motor Vehicles (Amendment) Act, 2019, the pay and recovery principle is not applicable to the case in hand.

Accordingly, holding that the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.50,000/- from the respondent No.1, with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization, I answer Issue No.2 in Partly Affirmative.
26. Issue No.3:
In view of the above findings, I proceed to pass the following order:
ORDER The petition is partly allowed with costs.
The petitioner is entitled to compensation of Rs.50,000/-/- (Rupees fifty thousand only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of petition till realisation.

The entire compensation amount with proportionate interest shall be released in favour of the petitioner through e-payment on proper identification and verification.
The petition against respondent No.2 is dismissed.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.2,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
